plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds erupt into slender spikes of violet-blue blossoms. Their sweet, herbal perfume drifts across the sun-baked fields and hums with bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to early August, peaking in July
plants.funFact: Lavender's name probably comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. The Romans used it to scent their baths.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest bloom in the protea family. It is a bowl-shaped flower head with a crown of silky, pink-tipped bracts around a center like a downy thistle. It looks bold and almost prehistoric against the winter greenery of the Cape.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter and spring, June to October
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. Its thick underground stem lets it survive the wildfires that regularly sweep through its fynbos habitat.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: Rounded clusters of blossoms in dreamy blues, purples and pinks. They glow in the soft light of the rainy season and brighten temple paths and hillsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early June to early July, during the rainy season
plants.funFact: Soil chemistry controls the flower color. Acidic soil that frees up aluminum gives blue blooms, and neutral to alkaline soil gives pink ones.

plants.name: Nymphaea alba
plants.description: Wide, glossy pads carpet still water. Between them, star-shaped white flowers with golden centers float open to the summer sun.
plants.location: Ponds, lakes and slow rivers across Britain and Europe
plants.funFact: The flowers open in the morning and close again in the afternoon. Their stems stretch to reach the surface, even in deep water.
